project.name: diplicity-react
project.description: Diplicity React is a React and TypeScript web application, backed by a Django REST API and PostgreSQL, that delivers a web version of the classic Diplomacy board game and is maintained by the online Diplomacy community. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: map-processor.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Builds one Parser per SVG layer, each configured with a selector, filters, a normalizer chain and a serializer.

nodes.name: converter.ts
nodes.summary: Element converters that rewrite SVG rect/polygon/polyline/line primitives into equivalent path elements, plus a factory that picks the right converter per source tag.

nodes.name: filter.ts
nodes.summary: Generic element filter wrapper and its factory, letting a parser pipeline drop elements by an arbitrary predicate.

nodes.name: normalizer.ts
nodes.summary: Normalizer stages for the parser pipeline: convert primitives to paths, rewrite element ids via a supplied function, and bake matrix transforms into path data.

nodes.name: selector.ts
nodes.summary: querySelectorAll-backed element selector and its factory, the entry stage of every parser pipeline.

nodes.name: serializer.ts
nodes.summary: Serializers that validate a normalized SVG element and emit typed map data — path, province center and text-label serializers built on a validated-serializer base hierarchy.

nodes.name: parser.ts
nodes.summary: Generic parser that runs the select -> filter -> normalize -> serialize pipeline over an SVG subtree and returns typed output.

nodes.name: center-parser.ts
nodes.summary: Extracts an x/y anchor point from the initial moveto of a path's d attribute, used to locate province and supply centers.

nodes.name: css-parser.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal inline-style parser that turns a CSS declaration string into key/value pairs.

nodes.name: path-transform.ts
nodes.summary: SVG path geometry utilities: parse a matrix() transform, tokenize path data, and apply an affine matrix to every command of a path's d string.
nodes.languageNotes: applyMatrixToPath switches over every SVG path command type (M/L/C/S/Q/T/A/H/V and relative variants) to transform control points.

nodes.name: style-parser.ts
nodes.summary: Parses an element style attribute via the CSS parser and remaps raw CSS properties to the map model's style keys.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Core TypeScript interfaces for the parsed map model — IMap, IProvince, IPath, IPoint, ICenter, IText, ITspan, IStyles, ISupplyCenter and INamesLayer.

nodes.name: printUsage
nodes.summary: Prints CLI usage help for the map parser.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI arguments, reads the input SVG and style map, invokes MapProcessor.process and writes the JSON output, logging per-stage timing.

nodes.name: MapProcessor
nodes.summary: Turns a board SVG string into the structured IMap model by running per-layer Parser pipelines and post-processing province/center/star relationships.

nodes.name: PathConverter
nodes.summary: Abstract base that converts a source SVG element into a path element, delegating tag-specific geometry to buildPath.

nodes.name: RectConverter
nodes.summary: Converts an SVG rect into a rectangular path.

nodes.name: PolygonConverter
nodes.summary: Converts an SVG polygon's points into a closed path.

nodes.name: PolylineConverter
nodes.summary: Converts an SVG polyline's points into an open path.

nodes.name: LineConverter
nodes.summary: Converts an SVG line into a two-point path.

nodes.name: PathConverterFactory
nodes.summary: Selects and instantiates the correct element converter for a given SVG tag.

nodes.name: Filter
nodes.summary: Wraps a predicate function as a pipeline filter stage over an element array.

nodes.name: FilterFactory
nodes.summary: Creates Filter instances from a predicate function.

nodes.name: PathConverterNormalizer
nodes.summary: Normalizer stage that replaces each primitive element with a path element via the PathConverterFactory.

nodes.name: IdNormalizer
nodes.summary: Normalizer stage that rewrites an element's id attribute through a supplied normalize function.

nodes.name: TransformNormalizer
nodes.summary: Normalizer stage that bakes a matrix() transform attribute into the element's path data and removes the transform.

nodes.name: QuerySelector
nodes.summary: Selector stage that resolves a CSS selector to an element array via querySelectorAll.

nodes.name: SelectorFactory
nodes.summary: Creates QuerySelector instances from a CSS selector string.

nodes.name: ValidatedSerializer
nodes.summary: Abstract serializer base that validates an element before delegating to serializeElement.

nodes.name: TypeValidatedSerializer
nodes.summary: Abstract serializer base that validates an element against an expected tag name.

nodes.name: PathSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializes a validated path element into an IPath with parsed styles and d data.

nodes.name: CenterSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializes a validated path element into an ICenter anchor point via the center parser.

nodes.name: TextSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializes a validated SVG text element into an IText, extracting tspans, position, styles and combined label content.

nodes.name: Parser
nodes.summary: Generic pipeline runner: selects elements, applies filters, runs the normalizer chain, then serializes each element to typed output.

nodes.name: CenterParser
nodes.summary: Parses the leading moveto coordinates of a path's d attribute into an x/y center point.

nodes.name: CssParser
nodes.summary: Parses a CSS declaration string into a property/value record.

nodes.name: parseMatrix
nodes.summary: Parses a CSS/SVG matrix(a,b,c,d,e,f) transform string into a Matrix tuple.

nodes.name: applyMatrixToPath
nodes.summary: Applies an affine matrix to every command of an SVG path's d string, transforming absolute and relative coordinates and arc parameters.

nodes.name: StyleParser
nodes.summary: Parses an element style string and remaps CSS property names to the map model's style keys.

nodes.name: convoy_path_through_fleet
nodes.summary: Checks whether a convoy path from source to target exists that passes through a specific fleet's sea province.

nodes.name: is_convoy_redundant

nodes.name: Variant
nodes.summary: The static map definition plus topology queries: adjacency lookup, movement legality, parent/coast resolution, fleet access, and convoyability.

nodes.name: Actions

tour.title: Project Overview & Setup
tour.description: Start with README.md to learn what Diplicity React is: a React web client paired with a Django REST API that manages state for the classic board game Diplomacy, live at diplicity.com. DEVELOPER.md then breaks down the running system service by service (web, service, db, worker, phase-resolver) and shows how to bring the Docker stack up locally. Together these frame the two halves of the codebase you will tour: the frontend in packages/web and the backend in service/.

tour.title: Frontend Bootstrap
tour.description: main.tsx is the frontend entry point: it initializes theme storage, observability and Sentry, wires a stale-chunk reload guard, optionally starts the MSW mock server, then mounts App into the DOM. App.tsx is the root component that composes the provider stack (React Query, Google OAuth, an update gate, the auth provider, an error boundary) and wires native deep-link and notification handling before handing off to the Router. This is the skeleton every screen renders inside.
tour.languageLesson: React apps assemble cross-cutting concerns as nested context providers around the router. Order matters: an inner provider can consume anything an outer one supplies, so auth and query clients wrap the route tree rather than living inside individual screens.

tour.title: The Route Tree
tour.description: Router.tsx defines the full navigation map with react-router, splitting an unauthenticated route set (login, register, password reset, email verification) from an authenticated one, and wiring per-area layouts, redirects, and error boundaries. Reading this file gives you a table of contents for the entire frontend: every screen you will encounter later hangs off one of these routes. Note how it leans on the auth state from Step 2 to decide which set to expose.

tour.title: Talking to the API
tour.description: The frontend never hand-writes HTTP calls. openapi-schema.yaml is a generated camelCase contract derived from the backend's DRF serializers; orval turns it into endpoints.ts, a typed client of fetchers, React Query hooks, and enum types covering every REST endpoint. axiosInstance.ts is the transport underneath: it injects the bearer access token on every request, normalises network errors, and transparently refreshes the token on a 401 while queueing concurrent requests. This generated bridge is why the frontend and backend stay in lockstep.
tour.languageLesson: Code generation from an OpenAPI schema keeps client types honest: the schema is the single source of truth, and regenerating after a backend change surfaces breakage at compile time. The API has two wire representations from the same serializers -- camelCase for HTTP clients, snake_case for in-process clients.

tour.title: Authentication State
tour.description: AuthContext.tsx exposes login status plus login and logout actions to the whole app, subscribing to the token storage store via useSyncExternalStore so any component re-renders when the session changes. The auth barrel re-exports AuthProvider and useAuth alongside the token storage helpers. This closes the loop with Step 3: the Router asks this context whether to show authenticated routes, and the axios layer from Step 4 reads the same token store.
tour.languageLesson: useSyncExternalStore is React's official hook for subscribing to state that lives outside React (here, a token store also touched by the axios interceptor). It guarantees the component and the external source never tear apart during concurrent rendering.

tour.title: Deep Linking & the Native Shell
tour.description: The web app is also wrapped with Capacitor and shipped to iOS and Android, so it must handle links that arrive from outside the browser. The deepLink barrel exposes deepLinkStorage, parseDeepLinkUrl, and a useDeepLink hook; parseDeepLinkUrl.ts converts an incoming URL into an in-app router path, accepting both the diplicity:// custom scheme and a whitelist of diplicity.com hosts. platform.ts is the small capability check code branches on to tell native from web. App.tsx from Step 2 is where these get wired to the native runtime.

tour.title: A Feature End to End
tour.description: These two screens are the busiest in the app and show the frontend patterns in concert. CreateGame.tsx is a multi-step flow -- variant selection, metadata, deadline and rule configuration -- that submits to the create-game endpoint from Step 4's generated client. OrdersScreen.tsx is the core gameplay surface: it groups units by nation, tracks order status per province, and drives order creation and phase-ready confirmation. The hooks barrel provides the shared building blocks (useDraft, useNetworkStatus, useRequiredParams) they rely on.

tour.title: Backend Foundations
tour.description: Now cross to service/. manage.py is Django's command-line entry point; settings.py is the central configuration module wiring installed apps, DRF and SimpleJWT, the database, CORS, Sentry, OpenTelemetry, email and OAuth, all from environment variables; urls.py mounts each app's URLconf plus the OpenAPI and admin routes. constants.py is the most depended-upon file in the whole backend -- it defines the shared enums and choices (game, phase and order statuses, durations, press types, reliability and commitment tiers, unit and province types) that every model and serializer imports.

tour.title: The Domain Models
tour.description: The backend rule in architecture.md states plainly where business logic belongs in this service -- read it first, then see it applied. game/models.py holds the Game model with its QuerySet and Manager: lifecycle (create, start, finish, pause), deadline and phase-frequency math, membership and admin logic, sandbox cloning, and event emission. phase/models.py owns Phase and PhaseState plus a large manager that resolves deadlines, NMR extensions, civil disorder, eliminations, and builds phases from adjudication output. member/models.py defines seat handover, nation assignment, and the NationPreference join. These models use the constants from Step 8 throughout.
tour.languageLesson: Django convention concentrates data-access and lifecycle logic in custom QuerySet and Manager classes on the model, so callers chain expressive queries (Game.objects.active().for_user(u)) and the model stays the single home for its own business rules.

tour.title: The REST API Layer
tour.description: game/views.py is a set of DRF generic views -- retrieve, filtered and paginated list, create, find-similar, sandbox create, clone-to-sandbox, pause, unpause, delete, extend-deadline -- and game/serializers.py provides the matching serializers with computed permission and status fields. This is the exact layer that openapi-schema.yaml from Step 4 is generated from, so the shapes here are what endpoints.ts exposed to the frontend. Following a request from Step 7's CreateGame screen lands you right here.

tour.title: The Rules Adjudicator Engine
tour.description: adjudicator/__init__.py exposes a single function, adjudicate(), which runs the rules engine over a variant and a game state and returns serialized options and resolutions. engine.py is that engine: an ordered pipeline of reducer classes that parse orders, apply legality checks, match supports and convoys, resolve strengths, and produce the next state. The adjudicator's own CLAUDE.md explains the design -- a pure, Redux-style model with eight code categories and hard rules for extending each. This engine is what Step 9's phase manager calls to advance a game.
tour.languageLesson: The adjudicator is kept pure: given the same variant and state it always yields the same result, with no database or IO inside the pipeline. That makes the trickiest logic in the project directly unit-testable against the standard Diplomacy test cases (DATC).

tour.title: AI Bot Players
tour.description: Games can be filled with LLM-driven bots. agent/models.py defines AgentTask, a durable queue of plan, finalize, and reply jobs for bot members, with an enqueue/requeue/reconcile lifecycle backed by Procrastinate deferral. agent/tasks.py holds the job bodies plus the agent.run dispatcher (with retry) and a periodic agent.reconcile sweep. These bots submit real orders through the same models and adjudicator you saw in Steps 9 and 11 -- they are just another kind of player.
tour.languageLesson: Procrastinate is a Postgres-backed task queue: jobs are rows in the database, so enqueue is transactional with the model changes that triggered it, and a periodic reconcile sweep can re-derive what work is outstanding rather than trusting queue state alone.

tour.title: Variants & the Data Contract
tour.description: A variant is a complete Diplomacy ruleset: map topology, nations, starting position, and victory conditions. variant.schema.yaml is the language-neutral JSON Schema every variant document is validated against. variant/models.py defines the Variant and VariantSvg models with visibility filtering and prefetch helpers; variant/utils.py is the toolkit that validates DVAR payloads against that schema, normalises and sanitises the dSVG maps, converts godip SVGs, and safely creates or replaces variants and their child rows. The adjudicator from Step 11 takes one of these variants as its input.
tour.languageLesson: A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) acts as an executable contract: content authors get validation errors before bad data ever reaches a model, and the schema doubles as documentation of every field a variant may contain.

tour.title: Containerization & CI/CD
tour.description: docker-compose.yml orchestrates local development -- codegen, the Vite web server, the Django service, Postgres, a phase-resolver polling loop, and a Procrastinate worker on one network. service/Dockerfile is a multi-stage build: a base stage installs dependencies, development stays as root, and production adds gunicorn, a non-root user, and staticfiles. entrypoint.sh branches on PROCESS_ROLE so the same image runs either as the migrating web server or as the worker. test-service.yml runs the pytest suite against a Postgres container on every push and PR, and build-and-deploy-service.yml ships the service to Railway on merge to main. This is how everything in the tour gets tested and reaches production.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Dockerfiles separate build-time dependencies from the runtime image, and a single image can serve multiple roles by branching in its entrypoint on an environment variable -- here PROCESS_ROLE picks between running migrations plus Gunicorn and running the task worker.
